title: Draft a support reply that keeps the facts
summary: Build a reply from a ticket and a policy page without inventing promises.
outcome: A reviewed reply that answers the ticket, cites the policy, and flags what it cannot promise.
body: A fictional customer has asked for a refund 19 days after purchase. The policy says refunds are available within 14 days, and that damaged items are handled separately. You will build a reply that is helpful without inventing an exception.
notice: Fictional ticket and policy only. Do not paste real customer correspondence into a chat app for this exercise.
prerequisites: The ticket and policy text below in the same conversation.

samples.name: Ticket and policy
samples.content:
TICKET: Order 4471 arrived on 2 March. It works, but I changed my mind. I paid on 27 February and I want a refund. I have the original box.

POLICY: Refunds are available within 14 days of purchase for unused items in original packaging. Damaged or faulty items follow the returns process instead. Exceptions require a team lead decision and are not handled in the first reply.

steps.title: Extract the constraints
actions: Ask for the purchase date, the request date and the number of days between them.
steps.expected: The elapsed time is stated and matches your own calculation.

steps.title: Draft the reply
actions: Require: acknowledge, state the decision, cite the clause, offer the next step.
Forbid promises that are not in the policy.
Require a plain-language version at roughly an eighth-grade reading level.
steps.expected: The reply is under 150 words and contains no invented exception.

steps.title: Stress it
actions: Change the purchase date so the request falls inside 14 days.
Re-run the same prompt and compare the decision.
Change the item to 'arrived cracked' and check that the reply switches to the returns process.
steps.expected: All three variants change the decision correctly without changing the prompt.

steps.title: Add the human step
actions: Add a line that tells the agent when to escalate.
Remove any sentence that sounds like a guarantee.
Save the final reply as a reusable template.
steps.expected: The escalation rule names the team lead exception explicitly.

variants.beginner: Follow the steps in order with the full prompts visible.
variants.intermediate: Try each draft first, then open the reference prompt.
variants.advanced: Write the reply yourself, then ask the assistant to audit it against the policy.

sections.title: Try a changed input
sections.body:
Replace the ticket with: “Order 4471 arrived cracked. I want a replacement before Friday.”

**Expected:** the reply switches to the damaged-items process and does not discuss the 14-day refund window.

checks: The reply states the elapsed days and the applicable clause.
